better_than_baseline=false. Baseline: BLIND A/B AGAINST GTA V: OURS LOSES all 4 pairs. Wowed: no.
- Pair 1 vs GTAV-06: GTA V has crisp pole and wire shadows, bounce light, sunlit pink cumulus and dense material detail. Ours has a pleasant warm facade but a CG-clean, evenly lit street.
- Pair 2 vs GTAV-28: GTA V has sun flare, layered haze silhouettes and long shadows across sunlit ground. Ours is a uniform warm fog with no cast shadows on the road.
- Pair 3 vs GTAV-22: GTA V has huge sunlit cumulus and bright ground. Ours has a dim shaded street, a near-black navy road and an empty cobalt gradient sky.
- Pair 4 vs GTAV-14: GTA V has a dappled altocumulus sky, haze-layered hills and textured terrain. Ours has an orange glare veil over flat brown roofs.

BASELINE: I compared all 16 fixed photos, the 7 gameplay photos and the 11 route shots against progress/img/baseline. Side-by-side montages are in /private/tmp/opus55/critic/lighting-A1/work/montage/.

Better:
- A warm, sunny late-afternoon look replaces the lavender haze: gameplay_01 has a warm facade, blue sky and pink clouds; gameplay_06 now lights the player and casts a long shadow; photo_05 and photo_15 have blue sky and water; route_11 is warmer.
- Crushed blacks are lifted (share of pixels below luma 0.12):
  - void deck: 48.7% to 8.9%
  - convenience exterior: 36% to 25%
  - route_02 hawker market: 34.5% to 18%
- Glass towers catch sun glints (photo_09).

Worse:
1. Cast-shadow structure is lost in several views:
   - photo_13 lost every dappled tree shadow on the wall and ground (ground shadow-to-sun luma ratio 0.59, baseline 0.23).
   - gameplay_04's canopy shadow band is softened (0.58, baseline 0.20).
   - Helicopter and helipad shadows are gone in route_08 and route_10.
   - photo_03's floor shadows are weaker.
2. Contrast dropped in 15 of 16 fixed views. Example, photo_08: luma std 0.303 to 0.206, 95th-percentile luma 0.927 to 0.669.
3. A warm veiling glare washes out about a third of every sun-facing frame (photo_07, route_06, gameplay_04, footage).
4. Colour is oversaturated. Sky HSV saturation in photo_02 and photo_08 is 0.51–0.54, against 0.08 in the baseline and 0.12–0.20 in GTA V.
5. Aerial water lost its sun glint and reads as a flat dark navy plane (route_09).

FUNCTION AND PERFORMANCE (all on real rendered frames):
- The 1280x720 route passed 13/13 gates twice, once with 10 Hz frame recording and once without. Both runs exited 0 with no fatal errors.
- The headless --test suite passed 103/103.
- Frame rate at the gates without recording matches the baseline (84–85 vs 85, and 69 vs 69). Draw calls are up 5–20% (driving 703 to 843, car entered 3310 to 3633). The fps drop seen in the recorded run was recording overhead.
- Footage: /private/tmp/opus55/critic/lighting-A1/route/route_lighting-A1.mp4 (150.4 s, 1490 real readbacks). I inspected the contact sheet and frame strips. The 72–75 s brightness swing is the scripted camera turning into and away from the sun, not flicker.

Judge: B is the clearly better frame in all four pairs, and no pair was close. The B frames show the same arid Southern-California world: dense, weathered and full of story, with layered aerial haze and lighting that its geometry backs up. Long cast shadows, contact shadows, sky reflections in car paint and rim-lit silhouettes make the sun position believable. The A frames are a Singapore-themed city with shophouses, supertrees and a Marina-Bay-style hotel, and they share the same weaknesses across all four. Large surfaces are clean or untextured: asphalt is a flat dark plane, paving repeats perfectly and roofs are flat single colours. Population and prop density are very low. Landmarks look like placeholders (wireframe-looking supertrees, cloned extruded towers). There are artifacts: hollow ring-shaped tree canopies from above, a pure-black median face, and a bare flat horizon where the world seems to end. The lighting gets the warm colour grade, bloom and some haze right, but it has few shadow-casting objects in the foreground, so it never shows the sun direction the way B does. A's best assets are its warm golden-hour grade and the ornate shophouse facades with lit interiors. The fastest wins would be material variation and wear on asphalt and paving, street furniture and vehicles that cast long shadows, more pedestrians, and replacing the greybox roofs and clone towers. None of the A frames wows. Two B frames genuinely do: pair 1's weathered liquor-store hero shot and pair 2's flare-lit, backlit desert inn. Pair 3's flat midday grass and pair 4's smudgy clouds keep those B frames just short. Note that the pair-2 B image carries a visible game-title logo, which breaks the blinding; my verdicts are based only on what is in the images.
